messages.author: c73bd0fa408650b6
messages.subject: Dodge error bars
parts:
Dear All

The following toy example shows means per group with error bars.

I would like to know if it is possible to slightly "dodge" both the
points and error bars to avoid the overlap in the error bars ?

I have played with position ="dodge" which works for the error bars
(although I have not managed to control the amount of dodging) but
anayway I can't manage to dodge the points.

Of course I could "manually" adjust the x coordinates per group but I
was wondering if there is a way to do that otherwise ?

Thanks for any help.

JL

xb <- c(0,5,15,60)
cpabs.avg <- structure(list(group = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L,
2L, 2L,
2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("1", "2", "3"), class = "factor"),
time = c(0, 5, 15, 60, 0, 5, 15, 60, 0, 5, 15, 60), cpabs.avg =
c(212.125,
146.5, 176, 222.875, 98.625, 75.75, 75.25, 130.5, 276.75,
266.571428571429, 271.75, 286.5), cpabs.sd = c(55.1243723644218,
53.04176252189, 33.2049910189933, 111.729824001600,
49.387498418122,
54.8810401817292, 59.386746958271, 67.1416413263781,
52.2787856455315,
45.504055287623, 55.761609937816, 60.4365074153978)), .Names =
c("group",
"time", "cpabs.avg", "cpabs.sd"), row.names = c(NA, -12L), class =
"data.frame")
p <- ggplot(cpabs.avg, aes(time, cpabs.avg, group=group,colour=group))
+
geom_line(size=0.6) +
geom_point(size=2) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=cpabs.avg+cpabs.sd, ymin=cpabs.avg-
cpabs.sd)) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=xb,labels=xb) +
xlab("Time (min)") + ylab("Mean (ng/mL)") +
opts(title = "Mean (SD) Values per Group",
panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())
print(p)

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Dodge error bars
parts:
Hi Jean-Louis,
You can use position=position(dodge(width=5)) #replace 5 with the
desired amount of dodging.

There is a problem with this though, which is that you can dodge the
points and the error bars so they will match up but, but you can't
dodge the lines, so the lines will not match the points. There is a
thread on this here
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/7e69f5db78d9cba8?pli=1
but I don't think anyone had a solution.

Best,
Ista
